scope: Confirmed component measurements from the additional production-speed work. No fresh two-hour video was generated.

imageTransport.scope: Image-only same-worker ABBA comparison on an RTX 5090. Batch timing includes image requests, waiting, download and validation; fresh process startup and warmup are outside batch timing and included in test spending.
limits: Two batches per transport; 24 matched cases are based on 12 prompts and two seed sets.

Three text-encoder cache hits occurred: one with original connections and two with persistent connections. All sampling and decoding remained fresh; the small cache imbalance limits attribution of the observed batch difference.
The comparison measures transport within an image-only batch, not a GPU-kernel change.
QC, story planning, voice generation, video rendering and complete-video throughput were not measured by this comparison.

projectSaving.scope: Local durable mutations of a 5.95 MB saved project in isolated temporary stores, two alternating pairs.
limits: Local persistence overhead only; these times are not image generation or complete-video timing.

oversizedProjectSaving.scope: Local durable mutations of an 8.80 MB temporary fixture made from the current project plus inert padding, six alternating samples per version.
limits: This padded fixture validates the large-file path; it is not a separately generated long production.

directorInputGuards.scope: CPU-only pre/post input-guard pairs, including two fresh complete project reads. Four alternating samples per variant and chapter.
limits: Only identical previously verified inputs can reuse the guard result; edits still use the original signature check.
The first uncached pair can be slower. These local guard measurements are not a model inference speedup.

shortFinalAssembly.scope: One local pair per shape, joining existing 720p30 media. Video and audio synthesis are excluded.
limits: Small assembly probes establish output parity in these shapes; they do not establish long-video or chapter-render throughput.

longFinalAssembly.scope: Final assembly of 7,200 seconds of existing 720p30 media: a 12-second chapter clip and its existing narration repeated 600 times. This is not fresh two-hour story generation.
limits: One baseline/direct pair, using repeated existing media rather than 600 independently generated clips.
Elapsed time includes FFmpeg subprocesses, file I/O and faststart; Python bookkeeping is excluded.
The avoided 3.02 GB intermediate would otherwise be written and then read again. It is not an additional saving to add to the measured elapsed result.
Native chapter rendering remains unmeasured here: its 120-second test did not launch because available physical memory was below its 1 GiB guard.
The one-pass path and its measured Join forecast require verified source format. Missing or unverified source audio retains the original assembly path and previous Join estimate.

budget.basis: Conservative GPU/disk lease accounting, including setup and warmup; not a settled provider invoice. Earlier approved benchmark spending is included once in the shared total.

interpretation: The percentages refer to their measured component only and must not be multiplied together or applied to a whole two-hour video.
Practical checks, production concurrency, source/reference inputs and the 12.3-minute voice estimate are preserved.
This hour made no new billable API calls, so it supplies no new Practical-versus-Strict or QC throughput comparison.
